clue.text: Natural setting in which to put silver, in this particular respect

indicators.note: putting something in a setting places it inside that setting's letters

blocks.note: an animal's natural setting is its home
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A jeweller describes the ideal mount for a silver piece, carefully qualified.
explanation.walkthrough: A natural setting for an animal is where it lives. 'In this particular respect' reads as one qualifying phrase, but only the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is public honour or deference shown to someone, a close synonym of respect.

clue.text: Husband, completely outstanding, revered

blocks.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband
all, as in 'all done', means completely
a debt still outstanding is owed

explanation.surface: A husband so remarkable that he is worshipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the husband, but it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means held sacred or deeply honoured, so it matches revered as an adjective.

clue.text: This part of US twice heard primary shock

indicators.note: heard means we go by sound, and twice says two different words both share that one sound

blocks.note: primary is main, and a shock of hair is a mane; both words sound the same

explanation.surface: Someone in an American region hears news of a big shock, more than once.
explanation.walkthrough: Both main (primary) and mane (a shock of hair) are pronounced like the state's name, hence 'twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a state in the north-east corner of the United States, so it is a part of the US.

clue.text: Shopkeeper sounded less refined

indicators.note: sounded means the word is spoken rather than spelt, so we want a word pronounced the same

blocks.note: a grocer is a shopkeeper selling food

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper spoke in a coarser way than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can mean coarse or vulgar, so its comparative describes something less refined.

clue.text: Prophetic work with unchanged line about what lies repeatedly in future

indicators.note: about means going around, so the earlier words wrap round the next piece

blocks.note: something unchanged stays the same
L is the usual abbreviation for line
the letter that occurs twice in the word future

explanation.surface: A prophecy whose lines stay fixed, concerning what lies ahead time and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What lies repeatedly in future' looks like prophecy talk but just points at the one letter that appears twice in that word.
explanation.definitionFit: The two Books of Samuel in the Old Testament are counted among the Prophets in Hebrew scripture, so it is a prophetic work.

clue.text: Dispose of lots, using element of WMD in battle

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here inside the battle

blocks.note: soldiers in battle are in action
U is the symbol for uranium, an element used in nuclear weapons of mass destruction

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a large stockpile by deploying weapons of mass destruction in war.
explanation.walkthrough: A(U)CTION. 'Lots' sounds like quantities of things destroyed, but here they are auction lots.
explanation.definitionFit: To auction is to sell goods off in numbered lots to the highest bidder, i.e. dispose of lots.

clue.text: Run as live broadcast, in general

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters get scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A TV producer decides to air a programme live rather than recorded, as a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means applying everywhere, which is what universal means; 'in' joins definition to wordplay.

clue.text: Wrongly ordered all the killing

indicators.note: letters wrongly ordered are out of sequence and need putting into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone gave the order for a massacre, and was wrong to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing as an adjective means deadly, as in a killing blow, which is what lethal means.

clue.text: Evil one mainly responsible for racket in state

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: ill as a noun means evil or harm
I is the Roman numeral one
a racket is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A villain is behind a criminal racket somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests organised crime, but it is just din.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is one of the fifty US states, home to Chicago.

clue.text: Drink with sailors in small club

indicators.note: in places the sailors inside the small club

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a ship's sailors are its crew
a driver is a golf club for long shots

explanation.surface: Sailors having a drink together at a little club.
explanation.walkthrough: The club is a golf club, not a social one, and 'small' describes it before the sailors are put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a cocktail of vodka and orange juice.

clue.text: Start of crossword clue, ending with unknown material

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: first letter of crossword
a clue is a hint
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: A solver describes how a crossword clue begins and finishes with a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed printed cotton fabric, a kind of material often used for curtains.

clue.text: Record piece of music

blocks.note: first meaning: to write down
second meaning: a single musical sound

explanation.surface: Someone makes a recording of a musical composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of music' suggests a whole work, but it means the smallest piece: one sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Note is a verb for jotting something down and a noun for a single tone in music.

clue.text: Some lesser vice manifested in private, maybe

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A minor vice showed itself behind closed doors, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In private' looks like 'secretly', but private is the soldier's rank, with 'maybe' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is the lowest rank of soldier, so one example of a member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Drinks diners combined with sweets, perhaps

indicators.note: things combined are mixed together, so the letters blend into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Restaurant customers having a drink alongside their puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer: these are drinks taken with sweets, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert wines such as Sauternes are sweet wines served as drinks with or after pudding.

clue.text: Feeling about male attitude

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the feeling word goes around the next piece

blocks.note: sentient means feeling, able to perceive
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Someone's feelings concerning men's attitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: SENTI(M)ENT. 'Feeling' looks like the definition, and nearly is, but the answer is defined by 'attitude'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a view or opinion held about something, which is an attitude.

clue.text: Irishman, for example, is on spacecraft that comes down

blocks.note: taken as written
a lander is a probe built to land on a planet's surface

explanation.surface: An Irish astronaut aboard a descending craft.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irishman lives on the island of Ireland, so he is one example of an islander.

clue.text: Still returning to ruined shelters, however

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so the word is read from right to left
something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: still, as in 'still better', means even
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Despite everything, people keep going back to wrecked shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like the definition, as it can mean nevertheless, but it is wordplay; 'however' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: However and nevertheless are both adverbs introducing a contrast, meaning in spite of that.

clue.text: Brutal emperor's final word of dominance over us

blocks.note: Julius Caesar's boast ended 'veni, vidi, vici', I came, I saw, I conquered
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cruel ruler's last declaration of supremacy over his people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over us' reads as rule over us, but over gives the cricket O.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicious means savagely violent or cruel, a direct synonym of brutal.

clue.text: King including rook and duck in place for breeding birds

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the king's name wraps round the other pieces

blocks.note: Henry, the name of eight English kings
R is the chess notation for rook
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A monarch keeps a rook and a duck in a bird sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: HE(R+O)NRY. Rook and duck look like more birds for the scene, but give chess and cricket letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A heronry is a colony where herons nest and rear their young.

clue.text: Artist appearing in American gambling centre I run

blocks.note: Reno, Nevada, is a US casino city
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A painter turns up at a casino in Nevada and takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appearing in' looks like a container signal, but it only links the artist to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter, so he is an artist.

clue.text: Again find something obvious about Mao's book? Just the opposite

blocks.note: surface reading: a plain fact about Mao's Little Red Book, namely the colour of its binding
setter's reading: state that fact with its subject and complement swapped, then run the three words together

explanation.surface: Someone rediscovers an obvious truth about Chairman Mao's famous little book.
explanation.walkthrough: Quotations from Chairman Mao is known as the Little Red Book; 'the cover is red' turned round becomes the answer, read as three words.
explanation.definitionFit: To find again something once known or lost is to make a fresh discovery of it.

clue.text: Vessel buoyant — what's odd in that?

indicators.note: odd points to the odd-numbered positions, first, third and so on, of the word just before

blocks.note: letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of buoyant

explanation.surface: A floating ship, and the speaker wonders why anyone finds that strange.
explanation.walkthrough: The question looks rhetorical, but 'odd' is literal: keep the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is a vessel, a craft that travels on water.

clue.text: Plague first spread around East

indicators.note: spread around means stretched to enclose, so the first word wraps round the next

blocks.note: the best comes first
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A plague that first spread across the eastern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: BE(E)ST. 'Plague' looks like the noun of the story, but it is the verb defining.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset is to trouble or harass persistently, which is what plague means as a verb.

clue.text: Jacket got from trunk, or put back

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the little word is read backwards

blocks.note: a bole is a tree trunk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jacket taken out of a storage trunk, or else returned to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage holding clothes; it is the tree sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket, originally Spanish, ending above the waist.

clue.text: From bearings, identified position close to fighting

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters come out of the words that follow

blocks.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A navigator uses compass bearings to pinpoint a spot near the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting' suggests battle; the answer is about boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside is the area right next to a boxing ring, the closest place to watch the fighting.

clue.text: Try again to find setter's anagram

indicators.note: the word anagram itself says the letters before it are to be rearranged

blocks.note: the word setter, letter for letter, with the possessive ignored

explanation.surface: A solver has another go at cracking the compiler's anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To retest is to try or examine again, as with a second trial of a sample.

clue.text: One lies in bed, reportedly annoyed by any noise

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the phrase is turned into sounds

blocks.note: oi is a cry of annoyance, and a stir is a commotion or noise

explanation.surface: A light sleeper is irritated by the slightest sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In bed' suggests a sleeper, but oysters grow in oyster beds on the seabed. Oi is a British shout of irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are farmed and found in beds, so an oyster is one thing that lies in a bed.
